items.title: 「贏了就是贏了」？Hyrox北京賽選手失禁奪冠為何引發爭議

items.desc: 朝鮮（北韓）士兵於2024年底被平壤派遣，與俄羅斯部隊並肩作戰，試圖擊退烏克蘭的一次攻勢。烏克蘭總統澤連斯基表示，俄羅斯沃羅涅日地區正進行準備，以接收新一批朝鮮部隊。

items.desc: 上星期六，達里奧·阿摩迪（Dario Amodei）呼籲放緩發展步伐,以「降低出現嚴重問題的風險」，奧特曼和馬斯克均表示認同。這名Anthropic行政總裁同時強調，任何放緩都必須有所限度，以免讓中國反超領先。

items.title: 中國強勢下，歐洲電池工業謀求「重新充電」

items.desc: 金磚峰會《新德里宣言》呼籲對伊朗戰爭「最大克制」卻不點名美國。而習近平七年首訪印度，中印關係解凍了嗎？

items.title: 香港支聯會「煽動顛覆」案：被告們的伴侶與戰友

items.title: 911事件25年後 美國機場安檢醞釀「鬆綁」
items.desc: 美國民眾很快將能再次到登機門送別親友，這是相關改革措施的一部分。

items.title: 香港記協主席訴《華爾街日報》解僱案 法庭判局部有罪

items.desc: The US-Israel war on Iran has shaken global energy markets and coal is no exception. Countries around the world are turning to the highly polluting source of power in a bid to avoid shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. According to the International Energy Agency, global coal demand is forecast to rise by ​1.2% this year to a record 8.94 billion ‌tonnes. FRANCE 24’s Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe has the details in this edition.

items.title: Keziah Jones goes symphonic
items.desc: This week arts24 talks to Nigerian Blues Funk Artist Keziah Jones ahead of his Symphonic premier at la Scène Musicale on September 29 as part of Jazz & Musique du Monde season. He tells FRANCE 24's Marjorie Hache about his music and about working with arranger Pierre Bertrand. Plus, we take a look at new releases by Beck, Miley Cyrus and Beabadobee.

items.title: How will EU respond to Russian attack on train near Polish border?
items.desc: The EU's top diplomat said Monday that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to "scare" off Kyiv's backers. "It is clearly meant to scare Western countries from supporting Ukraine, from going to Ukraine to show support," foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said, urging Kyiv's backers to do "the opposite". France 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

items.title: 'What makes China work despite the pain in society?' asks analyst Dan Wang
items.desc: In this edition of Perspective, FRANCE 24’s Stuart Norval speaks to Dan Wang, a China expert whose book ‘Breakneck:  China’s Quest to Engineer the Future’ is a New York Times bestseller. It takes a close look at Chinese life and draws from Wang’s own ten years of living there. Wang says the China and the US are some of the most similar people in the world, as they are both hustlers and take shortcuts.

items.title: French 2027 presidential elections: Why Gen Z has mobilised for Mélenchon
items.desc:
🇫🇷 French far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc #Mélenchon is both highly controversial and a #GenZ favourite.
 
Mélenchon's young supporters express admiration for his promises to stage a "citizen's revolution",  redistrubute wealth, fight #climatechange and support #Palestine. The candidate's critics have accused him of complancency towards #Russia and antisemitism. 
 
Despite being divisive, recent polls predict that Mélenchon will qualify for the second round of #France's 2027 presidential #election, where he would likely face far-right candidate Marine #LePen.
 
So, why has France's Gen Z mobilised for Mélenchon?
 
🔴 FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young voters to find out.

items.title: Should the brakes be put on AI?
items.desc: US President Donald Trump says he is worried about America giving China an edge in the Artificial Intelligence market if too many rules and regulations are put on it. In recent days industry insiders, including top executives at Open AI and Anthropic, have once again sounded the alarm, saying that the way AI is being developed could threaten humanity and calling for more checks to be put in place.

items.title: Trump criticises 'negative forces' seeking to slow AI development
items.desc: US President Donald Trump on Sunday slammed critics of artificial intelligence (AI) who warned firms to slow down development, branding them "negative" forces. The comments came soon after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced his company will not go public this year, citing safety concerns.

items.title: Climate catastrophe leaves Nepal mourning while the search for the missing continues
items.desc: The himalayan flash flood that devastated northern Nepal on August 26 was an unprecedented disaster. The death toll continues to rise, with nearly 1,400 people now confirmed dead and 5,130 still missing, including around 600 foreign nationals from 35 countries.

items.title: Was Russian train strike meant to 'scare' the West?
items.desc: The EU's top diplomat said Monday that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to "scare" off Kyiv's backers. France 24's correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg, has the latest.

items.title: Russia strikes Ukraine with drones as Poland warns of 'escalation'
items.desc: Russia continues its ramped-up air campaign against Ukraine, launching 453 drones in an overnight blitz. One drone struck 800 metres from a border crossing with Poland prompting the polish military to scramble fighter jets and helicopters.

items.title: Thousands rally in support of Brazil's Lula as election campaigning heats up
items.desc: With Brazil set to hold a Presidential election on October 4th, supporters of both incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula Da Silva and his main opponent Flavio Bolsonaro have been taking to the streets. Polls have the candidates, who are on opposite ends of political spectrum, neck and neck.

items.title: Dozens arrested as Turkish police raid LGBTQ bars, activists' homes
items.desc: Turkish police on Sunday made dozens of arrests in a slew of raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists. Authorities said the raids came in the context of the "Decade of the Family" proclaimed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, aimed at "protecting our children, the institution of the family and social order".

items.title: A 'complicated autumn' awaits Sweden after knife
items.desc: Sweden's general election remained too close to call early Monday, with nearly 90 percent of votes counted. Four opposition parties led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson held a one-seat parliamentary lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing bloc, which includes the Sweden Democrats, as both leaders said they were ready to govern.

items.title: ‘They drove us from our land’: Thousands displaced by Yemen conflict
items.desc: According to the UN, more than 86,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since July, following fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis rebels and government forces. Many have fled to refugee camps in government-controlled Aden, while others have headed to neighbouring Djibouti.

items.title: Yemen govt forces hit back as conflict with Houthis intensifies
items.desc: The conflict in Yemen intensified on Sunday, as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea and Houthis fired into neighboring Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen’s government. The Yemeni government vowed to send more forces to the Red Sea coast and one official conceded a “painful” defeat last week when Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: 'Palpable tension' as Philippines Muslim region holds first elections
items.desc: A predominantly Muslim region in the southern Philippines held its first parliamentary elections on Monday, seen as a crucial step in the long quest for self-rule after decades of insurgency and violence. Reporting from the region, France 24’s look Jan Camenzind Broomby, takes a look at the vote’s significance, as well as the tensions surrounding election day.

items.title: Retrial over 2018 France terror attack begins
items.desc: The retrial of three defendants linked to a 2018 terror attack in a supermarket in southern France that left four people dead begins in Paris on Monday. The defendants include the former partner of the attacker himself, who was shot dead by the authorities. France 24’s Luke Shrago has more.

items.title: Can Sweden restore welfare system amid increased defense spending?
items.desc: While the results of Sweden's general election remain too close to call, it looks as though the country's center-left opposition may get the chance to form a new government after four years under a right-wing coalition. The runup to the vote was dominated domestic economic issues, including the future of the country's once famously generous welfare state. But Sweden's international financial commitments - notably to increased defense spending following its decision to join NATO amid Russia's war on Ukraine - are likely to limit its options.
